subject.title: fix(codex): heartbeat notifications to other channels are silently denied by cross-context policy

question: Should Codex heartbeat, cron, and inter-session turns carrying the internal WebChat marker be treated as unbound for cross-provider message sends?
rationale: The patch restores a documented autonomous notification workflow but does so by removing the provider binding that activates cross-context containment; tests cannot decide that authorization policy.

options.title: Approve narrow unbinding
options.body: Accept the internal-channel plus turn-kind discriminator as the intended compatibility boundary and merge after a base refresh.

options.title: Require explicit authorization
options.body: Keep autonomous turns bound by default and design an owner-approved policy or authorization signal for cross-provider notifications.

options.title: Pause the fix
options.body: Leave the regression open until the runtime and outbound-policy owners agree on how autonomous turns should carry origin authorization.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow unbinding
recommendation.body: Accept the internal-channel plus turn-kind discriminator as the intended compatibility boundary and merge after a base refresh.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history signal ties this person to the internal-turn Codex message behavior introduced immediately before the regression.
